items.feedback: Right: the loop of choose an action, run it, feed the result back is the structure; prompt length, window size and memory only change what one call can do.
Right: the model only outputs a structured request (tool name plus arguments); the program runs the tool.

You assumed it would eventually succeed, but the agent is repeating the same edit and seeing the same failure, so more steps add nothing. The program needs a stopping condition, such as a step limit, that ends the loop and reports back to a person.

4 is right, but your reason isn't: the model doesn't run any tool. Each call outputs one tool request, the program runs it, and the result triggers the next call. That gives 3 requests plus 1 final answer.
Right: the result goes back as input to the next model call, so the model can decide its next step.

The name is part of it, but the model relies on the whole description: what the tool does and its parameters. Names can mislead (for example, check_calendar could mean read or edit), so the description is what it chooses from.

summary: You have the loop's structure and the model's output down. Two gaps remain: who runs the tools (the program, never the model) and why an agent needs a stopping condition. Redo q4 by writing each model call on paper with its input and output, then sketch the makerspace tool descriptions.
